stage1_raw_note:

* **Chief Complaint:** Patient referred by dermatologist for surgical consult due to melanoma on back.
* **History of Present Illness (HPI):** Melanoma on right inferior back, 0.7 mm in size, no pain or itching. Patient's mom noticed the lesion, and patient went to dermatologist immediately. No changes in lesion since diagnosis.

**OBJECTIVE:**

* **Physical Examination & Vitals:** One-centimeter shave biopsy site on right inferior back with no residual pigmentation, no other suspicious moles, and no lymphadenopathy except for a soft, nontender lymph node in the right groin.
* **Diagnostic Results & Labs:** Biopsy: Malignant melanoma, invasive, with Breslow thickness of 0.7 mm and Clark level 4. No imaging studies or blood work results mentioned.

**ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:**

* **Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning:** Malignant melanoma, invasive, with Breslow thickness of 0.7 mm and Clark level 4.
* **Treatment Plan, Medications, and Follow-up:** The patient is scheduled for an ultrasound of the right groin lymph node to assess for potential lymph node involvement. If the ultrasound is normal, further staging procedures may be necessary. The patient will be followed up with the results of the ultrasound and any subsequent staging procedures.

Please note that this is a summary of the patient's visit, and the actual SOAP note may vary depending on the specific needs and requirements of the healthcare provider and the patient.

subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Patient referred by dermatologist for surgical consult due to melanoma on back.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 57 years old, and I'm here because my dermatologist found a melanoma on my back and referred me for a surgical consult. I had a biopsy done, and it came back positive. Doctor: Could you please provide the location and size of the melanoma on your back, as well as any associated symptoms such as pain, itching, or changes in appearance? Patient: The melanoma was on my right inferior back, and it was about 0.7 millimeters in size. I didn’t have any pain or itching, but my mom noticed it when I was visiting her last month, so I went to the dermatologist right away. Doctor: Could you please provide the histopathological findings from the biopsy, including the Breslow depth and Clark level? Patient: The biopsy showed it was a malignant melanoma, invasive, with a Breslow thickness of 0.7 millimeters and a Clark level 4. I was told it was a superficial spreading type, and there was no ulceration or lymphatic invasion identified. Doctor: Could you please provide details about your past medical history, including any prior malignancies, surgeries, chronic conditions, family history of cancer (especially melanoma), immunization status (including HPV vaccination), history of sun exposure, use of tanning beds, skin conditions, and any prior treatments or interventions related to the melanoma? Patient: I don’t have a history of any other cancers or chronic conditions. I’ve had surgeries for my gallbladder and appendix before. My family has a history of melanoma—my mom and her sister both had it. I don’t recall if I’ve ever had the HPV vaccine. I work outside a lot at my auto repair shop, so I’m often in the sun, but I try to use sunscreen. I’ve never used tanning beds. My primary care doctor checks my moles every year, and he hasn’t found anything concerning before. This was my first time seeing a dermatologist. Doctor: Could you please describe any changes you

reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: 57-year-old patient referred for surgical consult due to melanoma on the back. Biopsy confirmed melanoma.

History of present illness: Melanoma was identified on the right inferior back, approximately 0.7 millimeters in size. The patient did not experience pain or itching. The lesion was noticed by the patient's mother during a visit last month, prompting a dermatological evaluation and subsequent biopsy. The biopsy showed it was a malignant melanoma, invasive, with a Breslow thickness of 0.7 millimeters and a Clark level 4. It was a superficial spreading type, with no ulceration or lymphatic invasion identified. The patient has not noticed any changes in the lesion since it was first identified. The patient has a slightly abnormal lymph node in the right groin, and an ultrasound is planned to evaluate for potential lymph node involvement. The ultrasound of the right groin lymph node has not been performed yet, and the patient does not know when it is scheduled. The patient has not undergone any other imaging studies or blood work for staging the melanoma. No sentinel lymph node biopsies or other staging procedures have been performed yet.

Past history: The patient has no history of other cancers or chronic conditions. He has had prior surgeries for gallbladder and appendectomy. There is a family history of melanoma (mother and maternal aunt). The patient is unsure about HPV vaccination status. He has significant sun exposure due to his occupation at an auto repair shop, uses sunscreen, and has never used tanning beds. He has annual mole checks by his primary care physician with no prior concerning findings.
